rows.claim: D-081: the frame is the scheduling unit for tick eligibility

notes:
Slice L10: 23 ratified entries, Status and Position only, read in worktree W at 2ea85438. Probe at /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/L10/probe.jl. Output cited as probe:<line> is the line of the P(...) call that printed the value. I ran it three times; the first two runs failed on probe-helper bugs.

Results: 18 findings, 0 unverifiable, 225 ok.
- 17 findings are drift. Each names the later entry that moved the rule: D-181, D-198, D-230, D-269, D-273, D-316, D-319, D-445, D-449 and D-460.
- The other finding is a § citation that resolves but points to the wrong section (L10-135, D-274 cites §13.7 where the stopped-sim services are §14). I guessed its class as deviation.
- Every lead has an entry:
  - Findings: `capture`, `event_budget`, `EventDeferred` and `stop_on` (both).
  - ok: OrdinaryDiffEq (prior art), ode23 (prior art), TraceHeader (the entry says it is retired, and it is absent from src), t_k and z_ (notation), ballocated (test macro).

Citation checks:
- None of the 23 entries carries a superseded → chain. All are ratified.
- Every D-nnn cited in a Position has a link definition, and every one of those entries is ratified: D-027, D-038, D-082, D-101, D-127, D-136, D-150, D-154, D-156, D-213, D-223, D-230, D-261, D-268, D-272 and D-449.
- Every § link cited resolves to a spec heading.

Open: one bug outside the slice, seen while probing. A BS3 tolerance refusal renders the wrong message. `BS3(reltol = 0)` throws ArgumentInvalid(:BS3, :range, :reltol, 0), whose message reads "t_plus must be a finite real > 0 whose end frame the run may take — the duration spelling". The `:range` renderer at src/diagnostics.jl:2507-2518 falls through to the t_plus text for any argument it does not name, so `:reltol` and `:abstol` get it.

Judgment calls:
- D-081 "frames = grid steps" is ok, read as frame-grid intervals.
- D-133's "localization_tol · h" and "four to six" are ok as old notation. h was the frame step, and the code divides by Δt_frame.
- D-290 "t* = tₙ₊₁ degenerates to the grid boundary" is ok, read as the step-end boundary.
